Each column translates by scrollTop × rate, wrapped modulo the strip height so the field repeats instead of running out.

01Background reads as distance: low rate, low contrast, soft edges.
02Midground carries the structure and takes roughly half the scroll.
03Foreground tracks the scroll 1:1 — anything faster reads as a glitch.
04Keep the spread under 1.0 or the layers separate visibly on fast flicks.

name: Counter Drift Notes
note: A sticky outlined display word slides at a tenth of the reading speed behind the text, driven by CSS scroll() timelines where supported and a scroll handler where not.
html:
DISTANCE

Studio note 07

Motion is a claim about distance.

Anything that travels at its own rate is telling the reader how far away it stands. Get the ratios wrong and a scene stops being a place; it becomes a sticker sheet sliding on glass.

Rate

A sky wants a tenth of the foreground's travel, rarely more. Past a fifth it reads as a second object moving in the same room, and the illusion of depth collapses into a shear.

Two layers at 0.9 and 1.0 look broken. Two at 0.1 and 1.0 look like weather.

Weight

Type is the heaviest thing on any page. Give the headline more travel than the body and it lifts out of the frame on its own; give it less and it drags the whole column with it.

Restraint

Three rates are a scene. Six rates are a fight. Cut until every remaining layer answers a question the reader was already asking.

M. Alvarez · motion desk
